# Provenance by Course

<!-- GENERATED by tools/gen_provenance.py -- do not hand-edit; re-run it instead.
     Every field is read from the build artifacts (laz/ tile names, dem_hd metadata, osm_geom.json,
     course.json), never from prose, so this table cannot drift from what was actually built.
     Verify with: python3 tools/gen_provenance.py --check -->

Exactly what data built each book. "Distributed" = built from open, public-domain and factual inputs
only, and handed out on that basis; "Personal" = do not distribute. This records what the build DID; it
is not legal advice and states no legal conclusion.

**Every book on this list is built only from:** OpenStreetMap geometry (ODbL 1.0), slope/contours
computed by us from public-domain USGS 3DEP LiDAR, par/yardage/handicap **facts** from published
scorecards, and — where an aerial or a missing green is needed — public-domain USDA NAIP.
No Esri/Maxar, Google, Apple or Bing imagery, and nothing from any commercial green-reading product.

**Flight dates are decoded from the LiDAR point records** (`tools/lidar_dates.py`), not from the
project name. Two courses were mislabelled by 1–2 years before this was measured, so the dataset
names below are taken from the actual tile filenames on disk.

**Geometry carries a date for the same reason.** Each row's OSM *extract* date is the earliest
`osm3s.timestamp_osm_base` across that course's Overpass responses — the instant of the planet data
they were computed from, read off the files rather than recorded by hand. The flight date lets a reader
judge whether the green SLOPE is current; without this one they cannot judge the same thing about the
hole and green SHAPES, and a re-bunkered hole looks exactly as authoritative as a current one.

An earlier printing of the club's card is reported to publish Black bare in the same way and to give the same verdict; that printing was NOT read here, so it is recorded as corroboration and not as a source. The book previously printed 72.8 / slope 135 for the Emerald tee ONLY, and the other five tees blank. That pair was not read off the scorecard -- the card's own grid prints no rating row at all, ending at the TOT column -- but off a line of prose on the club's website ('Back Tee: 6825 | Par: 72 | Slope: 135 | Rating: 72.8'). The USGA publishes 73.3 / 130 for that same tee. The two disagree, and the authoritative publisher wins: the club-prose pair is gone rather than kept beside it, because two different ratings for one tee on one card is worse than either alone. THE COLUMN THIS BOOK PRINTS IS THE MEN'S RATING, and every figure above is the men's. The USGA also publishes a women's pair for each tee, recorded here and deliberately NOT printed in that column: Emerald 79.8/152, Blue 77.1/144, Blue-White 75.4/141, White 73.5/132, White-Red 71.8/126, Red 70.2/120. A women's figure in a men's column is a defect class this project has already had to withdraw once, at micke-grove's Red tee, and it is not reintroduced here. The USGA additionally lists a YELLOW tee (par 56/58, men's 56.6/86, women's 58.6/85) which this book does not track, because it is not on the scorecard whose per-hole yardages the book prints. TWO LIMITS ON THE MATCH, stated rather than papered over. First, NCRDB publishes NO YARDAGE -- only tee name, gender, par, Course Rating, Bogey Rating, Slope Rating and the nine-hole splits -- so each tee was matched to this book's tee by NAME AND PAR (all six are par 72) and NOT by a yardage cross-check. The yardages here remain the scorecard's. Second, the NCRDB page shows no revision or effective date anywhere, so none is recorded; the retrieval date above is what is known. |

## Notes on the special cases
- **Seamless-mosaic fallback.** A few greens have no usable LiDAR ground returns — bayside holes over
  water, or greens under heavy canopy. Those use the USGS **3DEP seamless DEM service** instead of the
  0.4 m point cloud: still public domain, just less sharp. That service is a MULTI-RESOLUTION MOSAIC, so its sampling is not its resolution: at every green this project has taken from it, the tier that answered carries a source cell of **2.70–2.73 m E-W × 3.42–3.43 m N-S** — 3DEP's 1/9 arc-second tier at these latitudes. This record and the cards both called it *1 m* until it was measured out of the arrays themselves (`render_green.source_lattice`, no network needed); that was an overstatement of about 9x in area, and the cards now print the measured cell instead of a tier. Separately, **no acquisition date for that raster is recorded anywhere in this build** — `tools/lidar_dates.py` decodes flight dates from LAZ point records and this path has no point cloud — so a row's flight date covers its 0.4 m greens only, and the cards say so.
- **Holes that print no height.** Every row above counts three things separately, and they are not the
  same thing: cards that PRINT a tee-to-green height, holes that were MEASURED, and holes that were
  never measured at all. A measured change under **3 ft** is suppressed as level
  (`generate.py`, `elev_phrase`), because the two independent sources that figure was checked against
  disagree by more than that on some holes — so a measurement is not a printed number.
  Across this corpus **235 measured holes print on 161 of 270 cards**.
  `fetch_hole_elev.py` declines to measure a hole at all when any of these holds: the hole has no mapped
  centreline; its mapped line neither spans the card yardage nor belongs to a straight par 3, so the back
  tee cannot be placed; there is **no usable green surface**; the tee sample holds too few ground
  returns; the mapped tee pad spans more height than `MAX_TEE_RELIEF_FT`, so a median over it does not
  stand for a tee height; or the change exceeds `MAX_PLAUSIBLE_FT` and can only be a units or datum
  fault. **Which of those applied to a given hole is printed in that stage's run log and is not written
  into `hole_elev.json`**, which records only the holes that got a figure — so the rows above do not
  attribute an individual omission and this record will not guess one. Earlier wording did guess: it told
  the reader that every hole without a height had a tee that could not be found or had no ground returns,
  on four courses where that was not the reason.
- **Hand-added geometry.** Where OpenStreetMap maps no feature at all, its outline was traced from
  **public-domain USDA NAIP** imagery — corroborated, where the feature is a graded platform, against
  public-domain **USGS 3DEP LiDAR** — and tagged `_digitized`, whose value names the sources used. 20 putting surfaces, 57 teeing grounds, 18 hole centrelines and 76 bunker features are traced this way; the class and the id of every one of them is in the Geometry column above. Separately, one hole centreline mapped by OpenStreetMap has been EXTENDED the same way — the feature, its id and every other vertex are OpenStreetMap's, and only the added part was traced here; the Geometry column above names which part. Only coordinates are derived; no
  imagery is embedded in any book. `fetch_osm.py` refuses to overwrite a cache it cannot read, so a
  re-fetch cannot silently delete this geometry.
- **Greens rebuilt after the flight.** Where a course was reconstructed after its LiDAR was flown,
  the map is real measured data but may no longer match the ground. Those cards are labelled
  *pre-rebuild data* and the guide page names the holes.
- **Yardage mode.** Where no trustworthy post-construction elevation exists at all, the book prints
  verified yardages with **blank greens** rather than slope maps that could be wrong.
- **Jay Blasi routing diagram (Poppy Ridge):** only **viewed**, to establish hole numbering; never
  reproduced or embedded. Extracting factual hole positions is not copying.

## Sources in full

The table above shortens the Scorecard column to stay readable. Everything recorded for each course is
reproduced here uncut, so a claim can always be traced to what was actually written down.

### Bay View Golf Club
- **elevation** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR (CA Santa Clara County 2020, public domain)
- **geometry** — OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)
- **rating** — Tee ratings/slopes are the published course-rating values for each tee.
- **scorecard** — Official Bay View Golf Club printed scorecard (Golf ScoreCards Inc., rev. 10/2022): Black/Gold/Silver/Green per-hole yardages, par & handicap transcribed directly from the card (all tee totals verified: 6701/6153/5443/4711). Tee ratings/slopes are the published course-rating values for each tee. CORRECTED 2026-07-17 — earlier Blue/White/Red data was wrong (those tees don't exist on this course).
- **dem_source** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR CA_SantaClaraCounty_2020_A20 (0.4 m greens); trees from LiDAR canopy returns
- **decoded flight date** — **2020-04-14**, decoded from the per-point gps_time of this course's own LAZ tiles by `tools/lidar_dates.py`. DERIVED, not transcribed, and never read off a project or dataset name. Basis: points within 30 m of a green. The recorded elevation fields above name 2020, so the year this date carries (2020) is among them.

### Baylands Golf Links
- **aerial** — USDA NAIP, public domain (a U.S. Government work). Raster m_3712240_nw_10_060_20220519 -- NAIP 0.6 m, quarter-quad 3712240 NW, UTM zone 10, acquired 2022-05-19 -- served by USGS The National Map (imagery.nationalmap.gov USGSNAIPPlus ImageServer), identified from that service's own catalogue for this location. Used ONLY to trace the outline of hole 7's back tee (see sources.geometry); no imagery is embedded in the book and no other feature is traced from it.
- **elevation** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR, CA_SantaClaraCounty_2020_A20 (public domain), collected April 2020 at quality level QL1. The course reopened 26 May 2018 after a full reconfiguration of the 1956 William F. Bell layout (the club's own history page), so this survey postdates the rebuild by about 23 months and describes the ground as it is played today -- which is why green reads are printed here rather than blank greens.
- **geometry** — OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), PLUS ONE HAND-TRACED TEEING GROUND -- way 900000101, hole 7's back tee, tagged _digitized in osm_course.json. OSM maps only ONE golf=tee pad for hole 7 (way 786057551) against four distinct card yardages spanning 105 yd (Black 335, Blue/Blu-Wht 297, White/Wht-Grn 273, Green 230), and the hole's drawn centreline walks 283.99 yd against the 335 yd Black card -- 51.01 yd unaccounted for. THE MISSING 51 YD IS AT THE TEE END, and that was measured rather than assumed. In the hole's own frame (origin at the drawn line's start, +along toward the green) the mapped pad spans along -10.15..+33.41 m and cannot hold a 46.65 m shortfall; the next nearest golf=tee pad in the cache is 149.7 m away and belongs to hole 9. Behind the mapped pad, across the stream the cache already maps (way 786057536, dipping to -0.3 m at along -18..-22), public-domain USGS 3DEP class-2 ground returns from this course's own CA_SantaClaraCounty_2020_A20 tiles show a SECOND graded platform: a single connected flat of 222 m2 spanning along -45.8..-28.2 m and cross -9.2..+5.8 m, median 1.530 m (p5 1.265, p95 1.597), against the mapped pad's 611 m2 at median 1.559 m (p5 1.281, p95 1.649) in the same cross-band. The two cart paths the cache holds (ways 786057549 at cross +7.9 and 1364385367 at cross -10.7) flank it, and nothing in OSM covers it. In public-domain USDA NAIP it reads as mown turf against brown rough. THE OUTLINE was traced from the intersection of those two sources -- NAIP excess-green above threshold AND 3DEP ground above 1.25 m -- as a 12-vertex ring of 176.1 m2. THE METHOD'S ACCURACY IS MEASURED AGAINST THE PAD OSM ALREADY MAPS: run unchanged over way 786057551 it returns 459.1 m2 against OSM's 577.8 m2, IoU 0.777, mean boundary offset 1.44 m, Hausdorff 4.16 m -- so this ring is a conservative under-trace of roughly a fifth of the area, and the LOAD-BEARING dimension, the rear reach, agrees across all three readings (NAIP alone -44.50 m, 3DEP alone -44.50 m, the intersection -44.53 m). THE CARD YARDAGE WAS USED ONLY TO CHECK IT, never to place it: walked from the traced ring's rear through OSM's own dogleg corner and green end the route measures 332.7 yd against the card's 335 yd Black, a 2.29 yd residual, where the 16 baylands holes whose drawn line already runs from the back tee put that marker inside a mapped pad 12 times and never more than 2.0 m outside one. NO THIRD-PARTY OR COMMERCIAL COURSE-DATA COMPILATION WAS CONSULTED OR USED. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE: the card now DRAWS the back tee and its frame includes it (the ring's centroid is 36.65 m from the centreline, inside render_hole's 38.0 m tee corridor by 1.35 m -- a margin worth watching). The tracing alone did NOT fill hole 7's from-tee gutter, because that licence is derived from the drawn CENTRELINE's length; OSM's hole 7 way stopped at the forward pad, so the card kept its "no yd from the tee" mark. THAT CENTRELINE HAS SINCE BEEN EXTENDED to the traced pad -- see the next paragraph. PLUS ONE HAND-EXTENDED HOLE CENTRELINE -- OpenStreetMap way 786150435 (golf=hole, ref=7, par=4), whose TEE END was extended by ONE traced vertex, tagged _digitized with _digitized_part in osm_geom.json and osm_course.json. The way, its id, its tags, its dogleg corner and its whole green end are OpenStreetMap's and are unchanged; only the added vertex was traced here. WHERE THE VERTEX IS AND WHY THERE: at 37.4571141, -122.1159671 -- along -44.52 m, cross -1.30 m in the frame above -- which is way 900000101's rearmost vertex, i.e. the REAR REACH of the traced platform. That is the one dimension of the tracing that agrees across all three readings (public-domain USDA NAIP alone -44.50 m, public-domain USGS 3DEP alone -44.50 m, their intersection -44.53 m), it is bounded behind by a cart path OSM already maps (way 786057549 crosses the platform's rear from along -48.88 / cross -5.37 to along -42.53 / cross +7.87), and it sits on the platform's own centre-line: the 3DEP flat's cross-centroid at along -44 is -1.25 m against the vertex's -1.30 m. The along position of a tee marker WITHIN a 16.3 m platform is not resolvable from either source, so the rear was taken deliberately -- it is the reach the two sources agree on, and it is the conservative end for every distance a card measures from the tee, since a tee further back makes each carry and each from-tee figure LONGER rather than shorter. WHY ONE STRAIGHT SEGMENT AND NOT A TRACED PATH: measured on a 0.25 m 3DEP class-2 ground grid over this corridor, the back-tee platform's flat (ground at z 1.42-1.70 m, largest contiguous run per 1 m along slice, along -44..-31) has a spine of cross = -0.0332*along - 2.827 -- 1.90 deg off the hole's own chord, max residual 0.80 m over 14 slices -- and the added segment, which runs from cross -1.30 to cross 0.00, departs from that spine by at most 1.13 m (mean 0.49 m). There is no third feature between the two pads to bend around: the ground falls into ONE trough and rises again, no mown strip in NAIP deviates from the axis, and both flanking cart paths lie clear of the segment and are not crossed (786057549 runs at cross +5..+8 through this stretch, 1364385367 at cross -5.4 or lower). THE COLLINEAR ALTERNATIVE IS REFUSED BY THE GROUND, which is why the line bends at the old start rather than running straight: extending OSM's own first segment 44.54 m backwards lands at along -43.32, cross +10.34, outside the traced platform (which spans cross -9.58..+5.96) and on unmown ground in NAIP. So the route turns 15.09 deg at the old start -- and OSM's own forward pad corroborates that turn independently: that pad's 3DEP flat has a spine 13.71 deg off the chord against the existing first segment's 13.42 deg, a 0.29 deg agreement, so the pad OSM mapped is aligned with the line of play OSM drew from it. THE STREAM BETWEEN THE TWO TEES IS CARRIED, AND THE BOOK NOW SAYS SO. On the axis the 3DEP ground falls from 1.61 m on the back-tee flat to -0.50 m at along -22.0 and back to 1.65 m on the forward pad: a 2.1 m trough, 9.0 m wide at the +0.40 m contour (along -25.0..-16.0). That trough is the waterway OSM already maps as way 786057536, whose head node sits at along -22.79 / cross +0.05, and the 3DEP trough tracks the mapped line diagonally away from the axis exactly as OSM draws it. NO DRY LINE CROSSES IT ON THE AXIS: the minimum ground z over along -26..-14 is at or below 0.00 m at every cross offset from -16 to +2 m and first clears +0.60 m at cross +6 m, which is where the cart path crosses. The extended centreline crosses way 786057536 at along -22.35 / cross -0.65, 24.26 yd from the new tee. WHAT IT MEASURES: four vertices, segments 44.54 / 161.48 / 98.20 m, walked arc 304.223 m = 332.70 yd against a chord of 292.365 m, arc/chord 1.0406 (it was 1.0478). THE CARD YARDAGE AGAIN ONLY CHECKED IT: 332.70 yd against the card's 335 yd Black is a +2.30 yd residual, and no part of the geometry was taken from the card. NO THIRD-PARTY OR COMMERCIAL COURSE-DATA COMPILATION WAS CONSULTED OR USED. WHAT THIS CHANGES ON THE CARD: hole 7 now prints its from-tee column -- four rungs, 100/235, 150/178, 200/124 and 250/72 -- carries the Black tee mark at the traced pad, and drops the "no yd from the tee" mark, which is no longer true of it. It also prints one carry window, 229-243 yd over bunker way 786057548, which was withheld before because nothing located the origin it would have been measured from. AND IT DRAWS THE BACK TEE'S TREES: re-running the canopy stage against the extended corridor takes hole 7 from 67 LiDAR tree markers to 134, every new one of them between along -40.9 and +18.0 -- ground the book previously showed as open because no line ran through it. No hazard entered or left the hole's drawing corridor (3 bunkers, 2 water hazards, 1 watercourse, 1 fairway, 2 tees, before and after), and the other 17 baylands cards are byte-identical.
- **greens** — HOLES 3 AND 15 SHARE ONE GREEN -- a genuine links double green, not a mis-mapped duplicate. It is one OSM way, 786124069, of 1,507 m2, 80.3 x 31.7 m as its minimum-area oriented rectangle, against a 519 m2 median and a 47.5 m longest axis over the other 20 green polygons in this cache; the two golf=pin nodes standing on it are 43.8 m (48 yd) apart. Both holes are drawn on it and both cards are built from the one 0.4 m surface. The pipeline's one-green-per-hole check named this pair and it is answered in the record rather than waived: course.json declares shared_greens [[3, 15]] with its basis, which excuses that pair and no other. Nothing is missing that would explain the share -- all 18 holes bind, 17 distinct polygons cover them, and all 18 golf=pin nodes fall inside a green polygon, 16 of them one pin each. So no green on this course needed digitising from aerial imagery. Measured from osm_geom.json, except the pin nodes, which come from a golf=pin query this build deliberately does not cache. HOLE 14 HAS TWO GREENS, AND WHICH ONE THE CARD MEASURES TO IS UNRESOLVED. The club publishes that a player must choose the left or the right green at the 14th before teeing off, describing the left as a small target perched along the wetlands and the right as a forgiving punchbowl. OSM maps both: way 786096731 (397 m2) carries ref=14 and hole 14's only golf=pin node, and way 786096730 (315 m2) carries no ref and no pin and lies 30.3 m to the LEFT of the tee-to-green line, 374 yd out against 393 yd for the ref'd polygon (verified sign convention; 786096730 is therefore the LEFT green and 786096731 the RIGHT one). The card publishes ONE yardage set and one par for hole 14, headed 14L, and none for the other green. Its 392 yd from Black matches the ref'd RIGHT polygon to +1 yd and the LEFT one to -18 yd, BOTH MEASURED ON STRAIGHT TEE-TO-GREEN-CENTROID DISTANCE -- from the tee end of this hole's own OSM centreline to each polygon's vertex-mean centroid, which is the centroid geo.match_green itself binds on -- and on that same axis the 17 control holes have a median of -3.5 yd and a standard deviation of 22.4 yd. THE AXIS IS NAMED BECAUSE THE PAIR AND ITS CONTROL SPREAD USED TO BE ON DIFFERENT ONES: the spread quoted here was a median of +2.1 yd and a standard deviation of 19.4 yd, which is those same 17 holes measured on OSM WAY LENGTH minus the card -- a different quantity, and on it hole 14 is +11.4 yd rather than +1. Neither reading settles the question and the axis-matched one makes it less settled, not more: 18 yd is well inside a 22.4 yd spread. So the published yardage is consistent with the polygon the engine binds, but 18 yd sits inside the spread of the axis it is measured on and the printed letter L says the other one, so this is NOT settled from open data and is recorded unresolved rather than decided. WHAT THE CARD DOES ABOUT IT, WHICH IS SETTLED EVEN THOUGH THE YARDAGE'S TARGET IS NOT. The book DRAWS THE RIGHT GREEN, way 786096731, and says so on hole 14's own card: "two greens - drawn: RIGHT (punchbowl) - left not drawn". The choice is not made by the club's prose. It is the polygon that carries this hole's ref=14 and its only golf=pin node, it is the one geo.match_green binds the centreline to, and it is the one the 0.4 m surface on disk was measured on (dem_hd/hole14.json records green_id 786096731). MEASUREMENT AGREES WITH THE CLUB'S DESCRIPTION RATHER THAN BEING TAKEN FROM IT, through the engine's own render_green.green_summary and re-derived over every green on disk: that green tilts 0.14% and its shape_over_fall is 8.56, which is RANK 1 OF THE 252 greens in this corpus -- the plane through it drops 0.111 ft while its own p5-p95 residual is 0.952 ft, so the bowl is 8.6x the fall, and the card prints the honest consequence, 'no clear fall, overall 0.1%'. A green whose shape dwarfs its tilt by more than any other in the corpus is what a punchbowl measures as. NO INWARD-DRAINAGE PERCENTAGE IS RECORDED: that quantity has no owner in this engine, a hand-rolled definition of it gave 77.9% here against an 79.7% quoted elsewhere, and the two figures that DO re-derive exactly through the engine carry the reading on their own. The LEFT green, way 786096730, is the smallest of the 21 green polygons in this cache at 314.3 m2 (measured from osm_geom.json in this project's own NAD83 UTM 10N, EPSG:26910) and lies 17.3 m from way 786150403, a natural=water golf=water_hazard polygon and the nearest water to it by a factor of 7.5 -- the next is 129.9 m. Its height above its own apron was measured at 38.3 cm from the same public-domain LiDAR; that figure is NOT re-derivable from the artifacts on disk, because fetch_dem_hd.py builds a 0.4 m surface only for the green a hole BINDS to and this one is not drawn, so it is recorded as single-source in the same way the golf=pin separations above are. All of it is consistent with the small perched target the club describes; it is NOT drawn this round, because a second independent green panel on one hole is a book-wide change and shipping the bound green with the sentence beside it is the honest half of it. THE UNRESOLVED PART SURVIVES THIS AND IS NOT PAPERED OVER: the card's row is still headed 14L while the drawn polygon is the right one, and 18 yd sits inside the corpus spread, so the printed 392 yd is not proof of which surface the club measured to. That caveat is here and not on the card -- measured, the wording that carries it runs 61 px past the footer row, which does not wrap, it clips. course.json declares two_greens for hole 14 with the way the drawing must bind to, and render_hole stops the build if a re-fetch ever moves the binding to the other polygon, so the side the card names cannot outlive the side it draws.
- **hazards** — ENVIRONMENTALLY SENSITIVE AREAS: named on 12 holes -- 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 18 -- staked with green-tipped red stakes, entry prohibited, relief under Rule 17.1d. Facts from the club's own published Local Rules, which is the only source cited for them. THE SUPERSET IS RECORDED ON PURPOSE: the club's published lists have grown between printings -- an earlier card named hole 12 alone, the 07/24 card names 11 holes, and the current Local Rules sheet names those 11 plus hole 5 -- and the newer document supersedes the card's rules prose. Where the published lists disagree the book warns on every hole any of them names, because a hazard omitted is the failure this project refuses to risk. NO BOUNDARY IS DRAWN AND NO GEOMETRY IS CLAIMED: no source in this project's permitted set maps these areas -- OSM has no wetland, penalty-area or conservation way inside any hole's drawing corridor -- so the cards carry a WORD MARK and no ink. An ink would be a claim about where the line runs, and that line is not in the open data. If OSM ever maps one inside a corridor the build stops so the mark can be replaced by ink.
- **par** — Par 72 (OUT 37 / IN 35) from the club's published scorecard, which is internally consistent: the 18 printed hole pars re-sum to its own printed 37/35/72. CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE ARCHITECT'S OWN PUBLISHED DESCRIPTION of the reconfiguration, which states the design has five par-3s and five par-5s and is par 72 -- and the card's holes are exactly that, five par-3s (4, 8, 12, 15, 17) and five par-5s (1, 3, 9, 13, 18), counted here from the transcribed rows. OSM DISAGREES ON HOLE 13 and is the outlier: its golf=hole way 786150441 tags par=4. All 18 OSM holes carry a par tag and 17 agree with the card. If hole 13 were a par 4 there would be four par-5s and the round would total 71, contradicting both the card's own printed total and the architect's published count; the hole also measures 510 yd from Black. The card governs, because the published scorecard is this project's source for par. The OSM tag is recorded here rather than silently dropped, because the cross-check against OSM's own tags is part of adding a course and the result of this one is that OSM is wrong on this hole.
- **rating** — Course rating and slope as printed on the club's own published scorecard (07/24 printing), recorded in pairs and never half a pair. Five tees print BOTH a men's and a women's pair and the MEN'S pair is transcribed, so this column is one gender: Blue M 69.7/121 (W 75.1/131), Blu/Wht M 68.2/116 (W 73.4/126), White M 66.8/113 (W 71.9/122), Wht/Grn M 65.7/110 (W 70.3/121), Green M 63.2/108 (W 68.1/113). BLACK PRINTS ONE PAIR, 72.4/127, WITH NO M OR W BESIDE IT -- the card does not label it and this record does not claim it does. It is recorded as the MEN'S pair, and the sex is DERIVED from the same card's five labelled pairs rather than read off a label, because a longer tee cannot carry a lower Course Rating or a lower Slope than a shorter tee rated for the same sex. Three independent readings of that one card, all arithmetic on figures printed on it: (1) A women's reading is impossible. Black is 6680 yd against Blue's 6110 -- 570 yd LONGER over the same par 72 -- yet 72.4 is 2.7 strokes EASIER than Blue's women's 75.1. (2) The slope agrees independently. 127 sits ABOVE Blue's men's 121, which is right for a longer tee, and BELOW Blue's women's 131, which a longer tee cannot do. (3) The men's reading is ordinary. 570 yd for 2.7 strokes is 211.1 yd per rating stroke, inside this card's own men's spread of 174.8-222.7 yd per stroke (measured between its five labelled men's tees) and inside the 130-300 band tests/test_r17_yardage.py holds every tee in this corpus to. This is the method config.py already applies in this same direction for the one other unlabelled pair in the corpus -- 'a 5286-yd tee cannot rate 70.0 where 6026 rates 68.5' -- and it is applied here for the same reason: Black is the featured tee, and leaving the featured tee unattributed inside a men's rating/slope column is the shape of the defect this project has already withdrawn a book over. An earlier printing of the club's card is reported to publish Black bare in the same way and to give the same verdict; that printing was NOT read here, so it is recorded as corroboration and not as a source. No third-party compilation is involved in any of this.
- **scorecard** — Official Baylands Golf Links scorecard from the club's own website (print date 07/24, the PDF the club publishes on its Scorecard & Local Rules page): par and per-hole yardages for all six tees transcribed from the card itself. Every tee's per-hole rows re-sum to the OUT/IN/TOT the same card prints -- 3512/3168/6680 Black, 3192/2918/6110 Blue, 3041/2735/5776 Blu/Wht, 2862/2635/5497 White, 2751/2507/5258 Wht/Grn, 2536/2285/4821 Green -- and the per-hole pars re-sum to the printed 37/35/72. The rating/slope pairs are from this same 07/24 printing: see sources.rating. NO STROKE INDEX IS TRANSCRIBED: see sources.stroke_index. Par on hole 13 is single-source on the card, which OSM's own golf=hole tag contradicts: see sources.par. Hole 14's row is headed 14L on the card and the course has TWO greens at that hole, only one of which the card gives a yardage for: see sources.greens. TEE NAMES: THE CARD ITSELF PRINTS BLACK, BLUE, BLUE/WHT, WHITE, WHT/GRN, GREEN, and five of the six are recorded in the corpus's title case with the slash kept and nothing spelled out -- Black, Blue, White, Wht/Grn, Green. THE THIRD IS RECORDED ABBREVIATED, AS Blu/Wht, and the reason is the printed page rather than the card: generate.scorecard_panel heads its two tee columns with the name cut to FOUR characters (esc(fl[:4])), and 'Blue' and 'Blue/Wht' both cut to 'Blue'. This book is built on Black and Blue, so the header would print a column headed 'Blue' that matches two of this course's own tee columns and could not be tied back to exactly one of them -- the ambiguity tests/test_r17_yardage.py::page_vs_record refuses by name. Blu/Wht is not a new spelling invented here: the-reserve-at-spanos-park already records its own combination tees as Blu/Wht and Wht/Grn, so this is the corpus's existing convention for a combination tee whose full spelling collides. Nothing published is changed by it -- the abbreviation is a column label, the card's own spelling is recorded in this sentence, and the yardages under it are the card's BLUE/WHT column unaltered.
- **stroke_index** — NOT RECORDED, deliberately, and the slot in each hole row carries an em-dash. The card prints TWO handicap rows -- one under the Black/Blue/Blue-Wht/White block reading 17 3 5 15 9 1 13 11 7 / 2 4 16 10 8 18 6 14 12, one under the Wht-Grn/Green block reading 7 13 9 17 1 11 3 15 5 / 12 6 14 2 8 18 10 16 4 -- and labels both rows with the single word HANDICAP. Each is a valid permutation of 1-18, so the arithmetic cannot tell them apart. IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED THAT THEY ARE A MEN'S/WOMEN'S PAIR AT ALL, and that is the decisive point rather than the missing label. Every tee from Blue down prints BOTH a men's and a women's rating on this same card, so sex is not what separates the tee blocks; and the card's own guidance recommends a tee by DRIVER DISTANCE, not by sex ('Black 270+, Blue 240-270, White 200-240, Green Under 200'). Under that reading the two rows are one allocation per tee set, and NEITHER of them is 'the men's stroke index' -- so printing either under a legend that calls the column the men's index would be a false label whichever row were chosen. Omitting is correct under both readings, which is why it is omitted rather than chosen between. Anything about which row sits under which block is INFERENCE, not evidence, and is not relied on here. hole_cols names the slot stroke_index_not_published so the absence is stated rather than implied, and both rows are reproduced above so nothing is lost by not printing them. The book says on its own guide card that this course publishes no men's stroke index and that the HCP column is therefore blank.
- **dem_source** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR CA_SantaClaraCounty_2020_A20 (0.4 m greens); trees from LiDAR canopy returns
- **decoded flight date** — **2020-04-13 to 2020-04-14**, decoded from the per-point gps_time of this course's own LAZ tiles by `tools/lidar_dates.py`. DERIVED, not transcribed, and never read off a project or dataset name. Basis: points within 30 m of a green. The recorded elevation fields above name 1956, 2018, 2020, so the year this date carries (2020) is among them.

### Callippe Preserve Golf Course
- **elevation** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR (CA Alameda County 2021, public domain)
- **geometry** — OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)
- **scorecard** — Facts from the published scorecard for Callippe Preserve GC (par, per-hole yardage and handicap), verified.

### Trump National Golf Club — Los Angeles
- **elevation** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR (public domain), project CA_LosAngeles_B23, flown 2023-10-02 (decoded from the point records by tools/lidar_dates.py, not from the project name). Ground-return density over the 18 greens RANGES from 10.4 to 15.3 points/m^2 (median 14.7); holes 10, 13 and 15 sit at the low end, 10.4-10.5, about 29% under the median, so a single figure would be stated more definitely than the data supports. Chosen over the two 2016 Los Angeles projects deliberately: 2023 is the newest dense survey covering this property.
- **geometry** — OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)
- **rating** — Course ratings and slopes for all five tees are the USGA NCRDB men's values (CourseID 2594), which state gender explicitly: Black 75.0/144, Blue 72.3/137, White 70.2/131, Red 67.5/124, Gold 63.9/115. All five men's pairs are published, so no rating or slope is withheld here. Ratings fall monotonically with yardage (215.6 / 224.3 / 207.0 / 211.7 yd per rating stroke between adjacent tees), which is the arithmetic the club's own 2012 card fails.
- **scorecard** — Par, per-hole men's handicap and per-hole yardages for all five tees (Black/Blue/White/Red/Gold) are facts from the published scorecard. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS RECORD CLAIMED A SECOND, INDEPENDENT PUBLISHED CARD BEHIND THEM, AND THERE IS NOT ONE: the two places those figures were read are one publication on one host serving one table, so the claim is WITHDRAWN rather than reworded. A cross-check that did not happen is worse than none, because it is the reason nobody looks again. What does stand behind these numbers is arithmetic and open data. Every tee reconciles per-hole to its published out/in/total exactly: Black 3657/3214/6871, Blue 3347/2942/6289, White 3092/2726/5818, Red 2763/2496/5259, Gold 2362/2135/4497; par 36/35 = 71. Per-hole par is INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED by OpenStreetMap's own golf=hole par tags, which agree on all 18 holes, and the per-hole YARDAGES are independently corroborated by measurement off the OSM centrelines and mapped tee pads -- see the yardage entry, which is the second opinion this record used to claim falsely and now has for real. Hole 11 is a 223 yd PAR 3 (it was a 302 yd par 4 before the 2006 re-routing; any source showing par 4 there is stale) and hole 18 is a 503 yd PAR 4 (unusual, but consistent across every source consulted) -- both printed as found. Men's stroke index 11,15,13,17,3,5,9,7,1 / 10,8,12,4,6,16,18,14,2; a women's index is published too (7,1,13,17,9,11,5,15,3 / 10,12,4,8,2,16,14,18,6) but this book prints the men's, as the guide card states. THE COURSE'S OWN 2012 PRINTED CARD WAS DELIBERATELY NOT USED: its Black row fails its own rating arithmetic (differenced against the tee below it, 328 yd per stroke of Course Rating, outside the 130-300 band tests/test_r17_yardage.py enforces), its slopes are stale, and it stacks the WOMEN'S ratings under Red and Gold so they read as men's -- the exact defect that shipped on micke-grove and had to be withdrawn. THE BAR THIS RECORD ONCE PUBLISHED FOR THAT TEST -- "a normal 190-265" -- WAS A FIGURE FROM NOWHERE, and it is retired. Measured over EVERY adjacent rated tee pair in this corpus the real spread runs 141.8 to 284.0, and published men's figures fall OUTSIDE the retired bar at both ends -- so a bar this project's own books break is not a bar. The count is deliberately not typed here: this sentence read "all 45 ... so five pairs" and went stale the day baylands landed with 6 rated tees, which added 5 pairs and a sixth outside-the-bar figure (baylands Wht/Grn -> Green at 174.8 yd per stroke, which baylands' OWN record already knew and nothing propagated). It is 50 and six today. The band ENDPOINTS did not move, which is why nothing went red -- 174.8 is interior -- and this is the one sentence in the corpus whose whole argument is that a published figure from nowhere is not evidence, so a hand-typed count inside it is the wrong shape of claim. The rejection of the 2012 back row stands on its own; only the bar it was judged against moved, and a test now derives that bar from the corpus instead of quoting it.
- **yardage** — MEASURED against the ground, not only transcribed. Two published back-tee sets circulate for this course and they differ on nearly every hole (6871 against 7240 total, with holes 5, 10, 14 and 17 apart by 46, 102, 70 and 39 yd), so the set this book prints was checked using ONLY open data already on disk: OpenStreetMap's 18 hole centrelines, 20 greens and 86 mapped tee polygons (ODbL), plus public-domain USGS 3DEP LiDAR ground returns. METHOD. Each centreline is bound to its green by geo.match_green and the green's area centroid is the target. No OSM tee pad here carries a colour or a ref, so pads are assigned to holes two independent ways and the two are compared: by OSM way-id band (this course was drawn hole by hole, so a hole's ways occupy a contiguous id band ending at that hole's green) and by line-of-play geometry (perpendicular offset from the hole's axis, with the along-track term deliberately SYMMETRIC in sign so the assignment has no preference for a pad sitting at the line start over one sitting behind it -- a cost that penalised negative offsets would have assumed away the very confound being tested). 78 of 86 pads agree outright; the 8 that disagree are resolved individually, and in every case one of the two readings is absurd on its face (a 941 yd par 5, a 420 yd par 3). The played distance then runs pad -> the next centreline vertex -> along the line -> the green centre, which is how a yardage is defined on a dogleg, on WGS84 geodesics through geo.mlat/geo.mlon. RESULT: the printed set is the one the ground supports, and the agreement is across ALL FIVE TEE ROWS rather than the back one alone -- 88 of the 90 card cells (5 tees x 18 holes) are matched by a mapped pad within 15 yd, median residual +0.3 yd, mean +0.4, p90 5.3 yd. Back-tee residual against the printed set: median -0.3 yd, inside 8 yd on 15 of 18 holes; against the rejected set: median -10.7 yd, inside 8 yd on 7 of 18. Summed over 18 holes the measured back tee spans 6824 yd (pad centroids) to 6916 yd (pad rear edges, where championship markers sit), an interval that CONTAINS the printed 6871 and misses the rejected 7240 by 324 yd. THE CONFOUND WAS TESTED AND REFUTED, and it is the crux: had the centrelines been drawn from a forward tee, every length would read short and the printed set would win by artifact. Each of the 18 centrelines starts at that hole's OWN back tee pad to within 0.1-3.7 m (median 0.4 m), and NOT ONE hole has any mapped tee pad behind its line start, so the lines are drawn from the tips. On the four divergent holes the rejected set needs a teeing ground 38, 113, 68 and 34 m behind the mapped back pad; none exists, and the LiDAR says what is there instead -- behind holes 5 and 17 the ground is mapped penalty area, and 113 m behind hole 10's pad the bare-earth returns fall 28 m on a 60-83% slope into a barranca, where no tee can be built. TWO HOLES MEASURE SHORT OF THE PRINTED CARD AND ARE NOT CLAIMED AS CONFIRMED. Hole 10 has only 4 pads mapped for 5 tee rows and its furthest-back pad measures 316-321 yd against a printed 338; its Blue row (317) is matched to 1 yd, so the Black pad is simply absent from the OSM extract rather than contradicted. Hole 18 measures 485-490 against a printed 503. Both are 3-vertex centrelines across a dogleg, which cuts a corner a measured yardage follows, and neither residual points at the rejected set -- on those same two holes the rejected set is a further 119-124 yd and 22-27 yd out. So the card is printed UNCHANGED, and holes 10 and 18 are recorded here as measured-short rather than as confirmed: a pro-shop reading of those two tee plates would settle them, and nothing in this book depends on the difference except the two numbers themselves.

- **decoded flight date** — **2023-10-02**, decoded from the per-point gps_time of this course's own LAZ tiles by `tools/lidar_dates.py`. DERIVED, not transcribed, and never read off a project or dataset name. Basis: points within 30 m of a green. The recorded elevation fields above name 2016, 2023, so the year this date carries (2023) is among them.

### Wailea Golf Club — Emerald Course
- **aerial** — USDA NAIP, public domain (a U.S. Government work); USDA-FSA asks to be credited and is. Tiles m_2015621_se_04_060_20221110 and its sw neighbour -- 0.6 m, 4-band, EPSG:26904, acquired 2022-11-10 -- read windowed over HTTPS and rendered true colour (bands 1,2,3). THE SW NEIGHBOUR IS NOT OPTIONAL: the course's western sliver falls outside the se tile and reading only se returns zeros there silently. OBTAINED VIA NOAA DIGITAL COAST rather than USGS The National Map, because TNM serves no Hawaii NAIP; the raster is the same public-domain USDA product either way and the distributor is recorded so the fetch can be reproduced. Used to read the green cores and to corroborate the teeing platforms as mown turf; NO IMAGERY IS EMBEDDED IN THE BOOK and no pixel of it is printed -- coordinates only.
- **elevation** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR, project HI_NOAAMauiOahu_2020_B20 (public domain, a U.S. Government work), quality level QL1, 9 tiles, aggregate nominal ground density 5.01 points/m2. The horizontal and vertical CRS are READ FROM THE LAZ HEADER'S OWN VLR by geo.las_crs -- a compound NAD83(PA11) / UTM zone 4N with NAVD88 heights, vertical_scale 1.0 -- so no lidar_crs override is set and none is needed. THE FLIGHT DATE IS 2023-02-19 AND THE PROJECT NAME SAYS 2020, which is exactly why this project measures dates instead of reading them off a name -- four of its courses were mislabelled by 2-12 years that way. tools/lidar_dates.py decoded 2023-02-19 from the GPS time in the point records of all nine tiles, a single day: six tiles carry points over a green (08:56 to 09:20 Honolulu) and the other three cover no green and so are excluded from the range, though they decode to the same day. See lidar_flown, which the tool wrote and which is not hand-edited. WHAT THE POINT CLOUD ACTUALLY SUPPORTED, per green, because the aggregate density is not the density that matters: fetch_dem_hd.py measures ground returns INSIDE each drawn ring and holds them to a floor of 4.0/m2, and only 8 of the 18 greens cleared it -- holes 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 15 and 16, at 4.2 to 7.0/m2. The other ten measured 1.0 to 3.5/m2 (hole 13 the thinnest, at 1.0/m2 with 5.6% of its interior holding no ground return within 1.0 m), so fetch_dem_hd.py refused them and fetch_dem.py filled them from 3DEP's seamless multi-resolution mosaic instead. Those ten cards carry the coarse-data mark. NO SOURCE CELL IS NAMED ON ANY OF THEM: render_green.source_lattice looks for a resampling lattice in each reply and found none (2.1% to 10.5% of second differences at the float32 floor, against the 25% a resampled patch needs), so the record says the sampling grid is unknown rather than naming a pixel size that would overstate the resolution. CROSS-CHECKED, and this is the one figure on this course with a genuinely independent second reading: tools/verify_elevation.py compares each hole's measured tee-to-green height against the 3DEP seamless DEM and agrees on 17 of 17 recorded heights -- median |diff| 0.10 ft, worst 1.43 ft (hole 2), against a 10 ft tolerance, and the absolute green elevations agree to a median of 0.00 m and a worst of 0.07 m. Hole 17 records no height at all: its drawn line walks 312 yd against a 332 yd card, so its tee end is not the back tee and the tool refused rather than measuring from the wrong end. tz is set to Pacific/Honolulu explicitly because the engine infers a zone from a CONUS longitude band and Hawaii is outside it. COUNTY OF MAUI 2019 LiDAR WAS EVALUATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT USED. It added nothing at this task -- the 2023 3DEP survey is newer, denser and covers the whole course -- and it carries a no-resale condition the sources in this project's permitted set do not. A copy of the books may be sold, so a source that forbids that cannot be in them even where it would agree. HOLE 17 CARRIES NO ELEVATION FIGURE, AND THAT REFUSAL WAS INVESTIGATED AND UPHELD -- recorded so it is not re-opened. fetch_hole_elev.py measures 17 of 18 holes and refuses 17 because its mapped line runs 312.3 yd against the Emerald card's 332, a 19.7 yd shortfall past the tolerance of max(15, 0.05 x card) = 16.6 yd; on a par 4 the stage will not guess which end absorbed the difference. BOTH ENDS WERE THEN CHECKED AND BOTH ARE RIGHT: the line's tee vertex sits 1.5 m from the centroid of mapped teeing pad 900000571, the measured flat platform for the Emerald tee, and its green vertex is 4.16 yd from geo.green_centre of green 900000217, hole 17's north lobe of the 10/17 double green -- the same convention every other hole here uses. THE SHORTFALL IS IN THE STRAIGHT-LINE DISTANCE ITSELF, NOT IN THE GEOMETRY. Measured from each mapped pad to that green centroid: Emerald 308.3 yd against a card 332 (-23.7), Blue 289.2 against 300 (-10.8), White 253.8 against 269 (-15.2), Red 220.9 against 234 (-13.1). Three of the four sit inside tolerance and match the spread seen elsewhere on this course (hole 9 -13.8, hole 11 +10.5, hole 16 +9.2); only Emerald exceeds it, by about 10 yd more than the other three average. NO BETTER BACK TEE EXISTS IN THE DATA: re-running this project's own flat-platform method (class-2 ground returns, windowed plane fit, slope < 1.9 deg, roughness < 0.16 m) over a 300 x 250 m box extending 140 m further back along the tee-to-green bearing reproduced pad 900000571 exactly as a control and surfaced about 110 other flat patches; every tee-sized candidate near the right bearing failed on inspection against the NAIP crop -- one half in tree canopy, one sitting on a paved cart-path bend (flat, and therefore a false positive on slope), the rest off the bearing or in rough. The second NAIP epoch of 2022-01-08 shows the identical layout, so no tee has moved. AND THE HOLE DOES NOT DOGLEG: the mown corridor runs straight from the Emerald pad past the forward tees to the green, which sits just past the tip of a pond -- a greenside carry, not a bend. The forward tees are offset 27-44 m laterally, which is ordinary staggered tee-complex design. So the residual 20-24 yd has no candidate cause in USGS 3DEP LiDAR, USDA NAIP or OSM, and is most likely imprecision in the published card that this project has no open-data way to verify or correct. The refusal stands: 17 of 18 figures honestly earned beats 18 with one guessed.
- **fairways** — NONE DRAWN, AND THAT IS A MEASURED CONCLUSION RATHER THAN A GAP NOBODY TRIED TO CLOSE. NO OPENLY LICENSED FAIRWAY GEOMETRY EXISTS FOR THIS COURSE, and that is now settled against the record rather than against a snapshot. OpenStreetMap's FULL EDIT HISTORY over this bbox, 2007-10-08 to 2026-07-27, holds ZERO golf=fairway contributions ever -- not absent today but never created, edited or deleted -- and the same for golf=rough, landuse=grass, natural=grassland and landcover=grass. The query is proved able to see real edits by the control: golf=green returns contributions matching the practice greens OSM does map here. Overture Maps was checked and is a pure passthrough of those same OSM ways over this property (each feature's source record_id maps 1:1 to an OSM way id), contributing no fairway class; its land_cover theme is ESA WorldCover at 10 m with a generic grass class that cannot separate fairway from rough, green or any other turf. Hawaii Statewide GIS and Maui County were searched across roughly 280 layers: the finest thing carrying this course is a county ZONING polygon coded PK(GC) Park - Golf Course (public domain, State of Hawaii Terms of Use), three polygons of about 2.3, 72.8 and 358.2 acres covering the shared Emerald/Gold/clubhouse campus -- a whole-property footprint, no per-hole detail -- plus a single geocoded POINT per course in an infrastructure layer. The 1976 land-use classification predates the course, which opened in 1994. NOAA C-CAP is 30 m with no turf class. No golf-turf acreage was recoverable from the state water-use system. Commercial golf-GPS products do hold fairway polygons for this course and are DISQUALIFIED as proprietary compilations; none was fetched. Every other course in this corpus carries 19-37 OSM fairway ways. THE METHOD IS NOT THE PROBLEM; THIS COURSE IS. Validated against the five courses here whose fairways OSM does map, with rough sampled from turf provably outside EVERY fairway polygon rather than at a fixed offset, two channels separate fairway from rough well: local smoothness in the VISIBLE bands at AUC 0.802-0.974, and USGS 3DEP LiDAR ground-return intensity at 0.714-0.956. Near-ground return fraction and return height reach 0.62-0.82. Mower-stripe periodicity does NOT carry, 0.50-0.78. WHY EACH FAILS ON THIS PROPERTY, each by its own measurement: * LIDAR INTENSITY -- refused on Wailea's OWN data, so this null does not depend on transfer. Paired over the same ground cells seen by two flight lines, the cross-line bias is -787/+863 DN against a total turf interquartile range of 1,793 DN: about 48% bias-to-signal, where the labelled courses run 0.2-8%. 61% of the corridor is seen by more than one line and the paired-difference IQR of 952-1,518 DN shows the bias varies spatially, so no per-line constant removes it. The raster shows straight-edged wedges cutting across turf, trees and paths alike -- an artefact that would have produced a convincing false edge. Range and incidence normalisation (I/cos^2, I/cos^3) measurably DEGRADED the channel on every labelled course. * IMAGERY SMOOTHNESS -- separates MAINTAINED TURF from UNMAINTAINED GROUND, and only incidentally fairway from rough. It excels at baylands, whose rough is saltmarsh, a different material; it over-reaches at bay-view, whose rough is irrigated turf. Wailea is the bay-view case. A resort that waters its rough to the same standard may have no radiometric fairway/rough contrast to find. * TWO NAIP EPOCHS AGREEING PROVES NOTHING ABOUT CORRECTNESS. A second public-domain flight of the same tile was found and used (2022-01-08, 0.6 m 4-band, NOAA Digital Coast, ten months before the 2022-11-10 tile). Calibrated on the labelled courses, epoch agreement is uninformative: monarch-bay agrees across epochs at IoU 0.868 while being 46% wrong, because both passes see the same stable maintained-turf envelope. Wailea's 0.757 predicts a true fairway IoU of 0.43-0.58 at precision 0.54-0.82 -- about half fairway, half other maintained turf. * WIDTH FALSIFIES THE OUTPUT INDEPENDENTLY. The derived median width is 74.5 m, p90 116 m, against OSM fairway medians of 31.1-75.7 m on the five labelled courses. It is wider than every real fairway measured. NO SHARPER OPEN IMAGERY EXISTS FOR THIS PROPERTY, checked rather than assumed. Hawaii's 2 cm coastal survey is a shoreline swath and is 99.8% no-data over this course. The state's Vivid 2020 and WorldView-2 layers and the USGS High Resolution State Orthoimagery are all Maxar/DigitalGlobe-sourced and disqualified, with the USGS copies dead-linked. OpenAerialMap's only non-Maxar Maui item covers Lahaina. Maui County publishes no imagery. Public-domain USDA NAIP at 0.6 m is the ceiling here. A TURF CORRIDOR WAS BUILT, RENDERED, LOOKED AT AND REMOVED. It was the maintained turf within 28 m of each centreline: 33-61 m wide, edge good to only 10-15 m, and its boundary followed nothing on the ground -- on inspection its long edges were the two TREE LINES, the gap between them rather than a mowing line. Hand-tracing was then attempted on the clearest hole, whose mower striping is genuinely visible at high zoom, and refused for the same reason: the striped texture can be seen but no boundary can be placed on it, because the only resolvable edges at hole scale are trees, cart paths, bunkers and the road. Drawing one would have been an estimate presented as a measurement. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: OSM gaining the ways, imagery sharp enough to resolve individual mowing passes, or a LiDAR flight radiometrically consistent between lines. WHAT MAY NOT BE USED, and this is a legal limit rather than a technical one: the club's own course map or hole diagrams, which are copyrighted artwork and layout, and Google, Apple, Bing, Esri or Maxar imagery. Tracing any of those would make the geometry a derivative of them and would falsify this record. The published scorecard is legitimately usable and carries par, yardage and handicap, but no geometry at all -- it can check a length once a shape exists by other means and can never supply one.
- **geometry** — OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0) for the fetched cache, PLUS HAND-READ FEATURES DIGITISED FROM PUBLIC-DOMAIN USDA NAIP AND PUBLIC-DOMAIN USGS 3DEP LiDAR, every one of them tagged _digitized in the caches so a machine can tell them from OSM's own. This is the same act, and the same marker, as bay-view's two greens (ways 900000005 and 900000007) and baylands hole 7's back-tee pad (way 900000101). WHAT OSM HAS AND HAS NOT MAPPED HERE. OSM maps the Emerald Course's own leisure=golf_course boundary (way 336932921, name='Wailea Emerald Course') and it maps no golf=green, no golf=hole, no golf=tee and no golf=bunker for this course at all. So every green ring, every hole centreline and every teeing ground in these caches was read here from open imagery and open LiDAR; nothing was copied from any third-party or commercial compilation of course data, and none was consulted. THE BOUNDARY IS NOT USED TO CLIP, AND THAT IS A CORRECTNESS DECISION RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE. HOLE 1 LIES OUTSIDE WAY 336932921 -- south of Wailea Golf Club Drive, on ground OSM's crude course polygons assign to the Gold Course. Clipping this course to its own OSM boundary would silently drop a hole, which is the failure this project refuses above all others, so the boundary is carried for orientation only and osm_bbox starts from that way's own bounding box (20.6657695/-156.440397/20.6757067/-156.4320219) widened by roughly 0.0015 deg (~165 m) on every side, AND IS THEN EXTENDED 78 m FURTHER SOUTH, to [20.6636, -156.4419, 20.6772, -156.4305]. The extension is measured, not padding: tools/check_osm_bbox.py requires every printed hole's drawing corridor -- render_hole.DRAW_CORRIDOR_M, 68 m -- to lie inside the box the caches record being FETCHED with, and hole 1's Emerald teeing point at 20.664523 sat 43.3 m short of that on the southern edge, precisely because hole 1 is the hole that lies outside the boundary way. The other three edges already cleared it by 132-145 m and are unchanged, so the box only ever grew. All three caches were re-fetched against the widened box and all three record it. GREENS: 18 rings, one per hole, each a CORE inside the putting surface and NOT an outline -- see green_outline_unestablished_basis for the three readings that say no edge is establishable here, and for what every card therefore withholds. TEEING GROUNDS: the routing solve measured a teeing platform for each of the four physical tee sets on each hole -- 72 in all -- and 16 of the 72 are INFERRED rather than measured: they were derived along the measured hole axis at the card distance from the measured green centre, which makes them a restatement of the scorecard and not an independent measurement of the ground. THEY ARE NOT DRAWN. Only the 56 VERIFIED pads appear in osm_course.json. Of the 16 inferred, the count that have no detected flat platform beneath them at all depends on where the threshold is put and so is published with its threshold: 7 sit at on_flat_platform exactly 0.00 (hole 2 Emerald, hole 4 White, hole 10 Blue, hole 10 White, hole 14 Emerald, hole 15 Emerald, hole 15 Blue) and 9 sit below 0.05. The full inferred list, as hole and tee: 2 Emerald, 3 Emerald, 3 Blue, 4 Blue, 4 White, 4 Red, 8 Emerald, 10 Blue, 10 White, 12 Emerald, 13 Emerald, 14 Emerald, 15 Emerald, 15 Blue, 16 Blue, 18 Blue. WHAT THAT COSTS THE CARDS, MEASURED ON THE CARDS THEMSELVES rather than assumed from the gate names. The EMERALD (back) tee is inferred on 7 holes -- 2, 3, 8, 12, 13, 14 and 15 -- so on those holes no teeing-ground POLYGON is drawn (the inferred pads are not in the cache at all: render_hole's published tee_pad_rear_yd is 0.00 on every one of them, against 8.4 to 11.2 yd where a measured pad does sit under the line's start). BUT THE CARD STILL PRINTS THE 'EME' TEE MARK ON THEM, and that is stated here because it is the one place this course's inferred geometry reaches paper. render_hole marks the start of the drawn line whenever the drawn length agrees with the card, which on an inferred hole it does BY CONSTRUCTION -- the point was placed at the card distance, so arc and card agree to 0.09-0.17 yd and the agreement is arithmetic rather than evidence. So on those 7 cards the tee mark says 'the card says you play from about here, on the measured line of this hole', not 'a teeing platform was surveyed here', and the from-the-tee gutter beside it restates the scorecard rather than measuring the ground. The other 11 holes start their line inside a measured platform, and on those the same mark and the same gutter are measurements. HOLE 17 PRINTS NEITHER: its drawn line walks 312 yd against a 332 yd card, a 19.74 yd shortfall past render_hole's own bar, so it draws no tee mark, prints no from-the-tee spans, and (see sources.elevation) records no tee-to-green height either -- the engine refusing on its own, which is the behaviour this record relies on rather than a gap in it. CENTRELINES: 18 two-vertex ways, each running from that hole's Emerald teeing point to its green core's measured centre. NO DOGLEG IS ASSERTED ANYWHERE ON THIS COURSE, and that is a measurement rather than an omission: the four par 3s cannot dogleg and they set the straight-line noise floor at +1.3 to +15.9 m, and no par 4 or 5 exceeds it except hole 9 at +17.2 m, which is inside it. So a bend would have to beat a floor no hole beats, and every line is drawn straight. PAD SHAPES ARE SQUARES OF THE MEASURED AREA, NOT TRACED OUTLINES, and every pad's own _digitized tag says so in those words -- no new tag key was invented for it, because gen_provenance and the OSM vocabulary tests read _digitized and a key nothing reads would be a claim nothing audits. What is measured is each platform's CENTROID and its AREA, both from the public-domain 3DEP bare-earth surface; its outline was not traced, and a square of the right area at the right centre is the least the drawing can claim while still marking the tee. No distance on any card is measured from a pad's edge -- the centrelines start at the measured centroid -- so the square's shape enters no printed figure.
- **greens** — 15 MEASURED OUTLINES and 3 CORES (holes 11, 13 and 16), one polygon per hole -- see green_outline_unestablished_basis, which owns that finding and every figure behind it, including why all eighteen still withhold their printed depth and width and why the reason differs between the fifteen and the three. HOLE 6 NO LONGER WITHHOLDS ITS PLANE, and the reason is worth recording because the earlier withholding rested on a premise that measurement overturned. It was withheld on the basis that the green's 'northern (back) part' reached about 20 deg, so a plane would understate the back. Measured against the new outline: ZERO 3DEP cells at or above 18 deg fall inside it, on BOTH the class-2 point cloud and the seamless mosaic independently; the nearest such cell is 1.02 m OUTSIDE the ring and their median is 20.8 m outside; and they are not a northern feature at all but a ring around the pad on all eight octants, concentrated to the WEST (184 cells at or above 15 deg within 6 m) with 96 of their own across the front. That ground is the fall-off around a green pad built on a hillside -- a bank, never putting surface -- and near-infrared separates it from the mown surface by 18.6 DN against the three OSM-mapped putting surfaces on this property as the yardstick. Inside the outline the maximum is 13.1 deg, on 4 of 1,018 cells, all at or within 0.6 m of the boundary. The result survives buffering the ring outward by 1.0 m, nearly twice the corrected 0.55 m edge bias. THE OLD CORROBORATING FIGURE IS NOT DIAGNOSTIC, and the reason is measured rather than argued. The withholding cited an interior mean of 4.70 deg as 'the steepest of the nine cores'. Running the IDENTICAL lattice over the three OSM-mapped real putting surfaces on this property returns 3.90, 4.18 and 7.74 deg -- so 4.70 sits inside the range genuine greens produce on that raster and cannot separate putting surface from anything else. (An earlier draft of this note blamed nearest-fill and single-shot scatter for the excess. That mechanism is REFUTED: at 0.3 m separation hole 6 is the 13th smoothest of 18, its close-pair height difference is the course median, and void fraction correlates -0.33 with per-cell slope, the wrong sign. What is actually there is genuine undulation of about 4.5 cm rms at 1-1.5 m support -- 35.5 mm at 1.5 m against a course median of 24.6, the largest of any green here. It is recorded as a PROPERTY of this green, not a doubt about it: 4.5 cm sits below the card's own 15 cm contour interval, so no rendering choice conceals it, and it is isotropic across all eight octants, so it biases the plane in no direction. Injection tests bound any hidden tier at about 25 cm.) WHAT THE CORE ACTUALLY GOT WRONG WAS DIRECTION, not steepness, and this is the real reason the withholding existed. Run through the build's own plane machinery on the build's own surface, the 73 m2 core yields 1.4% feeding BACK-LEFT at 293.6 deg, while the 368.9 m2 outline yields about 1.1% feeding FRONT at 179.3 deg. Both public-domain surfaces agree independently -- the seamless mosaic and the raw class-2 returns put the outline at 179.3 and 182.7 deg and the core at 293.6 and 275.4 deg. The core's plane therefore named the WRONG SIDE of the green by 114-118 deg: a card built on it would tell a player the ball feeds away from them when it feeds toward them. That is a far stronger reason to distrust the core than the one originally recorded, and refitting to the outline is what cures it -- which is why the fix was to re-digitise way 900000206 to the measured outline and rebuild the surface, not to flip a flag. Hole 6 does steepen from front to back (+0.86 deg), but that ranks 7th of 18 here, six greens are steeper front-to-back -- hole 13 at 3.04 deg -- and every one of them prints a plane. HOLES 10 AND 17 SHARE ONE PUTTING SURFACE -- a double green of about 1,260 m2 fronted by a lake, with the OSM lake sitting immediately west of the measured surface. The area figure is the one to keep: the raw near-infrared extraction measures 1,137.9 m2, which is 9-10% low by the 0.55 m inward edge bias measured twice independently, and three routes to the corrected value give 1,238, 1,248 and 1,261 m2. IT IS NOT DECLARED UNDER shared_greens, AND THE REASON MATTERS. That key exists for two holes bound to ONE polygon, where a plane fitted across the polygon measures the step BETWEEN the lobes and belongs to neither hole. Here each hole has its OWN measured lobe, cut with the neck between them excluded from both, so each card's plane is fitted to the lobe that hole actually plays and neither read crosses the neck. The cut is derived, not drawn: rasterising the interior at 0.15 m, taking the Euclidean distance transform and inserting cells into a union-find in order of decreasing distance, the neck is the single merge that maximises the smaller of the two components joined -- it joins 501.5 and 270.6 m2 where the runner-up joins 0.2 and 26.8 m2, so the rule is nowhere near ambiguous. The throat is 4.10 m wide; the excluded band is the interval over which the surface is no wider than twice its own throat, 7.9 m along the axis and 48.3 m2, 4.2% of the surface. That band is measurably the step: its bare-earth median slope is 7.1 deg against 2.9 deg in hole 10's lobe and 2.6 deg in hole 17's, and the 16.2 deg maximum this record used to publish for the shared surface lies IN THE NECK, in neither hole's green. Hole 10 takes the south lobe (754 m2 corrected) and hole 17 the north (441 m2), assigned by geometry rather than assumption: hole 10's centreline passes 0.84 m from the south lobe's centroid against 21.74 m from the north, and its tee-to-green ray enters the south lobe and never the north. The published scorecard confirms the assignment rather than merely permitting it -- hole 10's Emerald residual is -2.5 yd with this assignment and +37.9 yd with the lobes swapped. The imagery reproduces the split unaided: at an anchor drop one DN tighter than the published member the near-infrared closes the throat by itself and returns two separate surfaces, 98% and 99% of which fall inside the two derived lobes. The lobe centroids are 41.9 m apart, so geo.match_green binds each hole to a distinct polygon and geo.assert_one_green_per_hole sees no clash to excuse. Declaring shared_greens here would withhold two correct lobe reads to cure a defect this geometry does not have. The share is recorded here rather than in a key because it is a fact about the ground a reader should know, not a waiver the build needs.
- **hazards** — 76 BUNKERS ARE DRAWN, AND NONE OF THEM COMES FROM OPENSTREETMAP. OSM carries no golf=bunker way for the Emerald Course at all -- the three golf=bunker ways inside the fetch box lie 150-272 m from every Emerald hole's tee-to-green line, and Emerald 18, the nearest hole, is straight to within 6.7 m, so no dogleg brings them near; they belong to adjoining Wailea ground caught by the same tile. Until this build every card printed 0B on all eighteen holes, which on a course built around its bunkering reads as open ground and is the omission CLAUDE.md rule 1 forbids outright. HOW THEY WERE DERIVED, all of it from public-domain sources. Sand was found in public-domain USDA NAIP 0.6 m 4-band, tiles m_2015621_se_04_060_20221110 and its sw neighbour, flown 2022-11-10, EPSG:26904, calibrated on 1,237 sand pixels against 9,000 matched non-sand pixels drawn in equal parts from vegetation, cart path and bare ground. Visible brightness was the best single discriminant at AUC 0.83, ahead of near-infrared at 0.71 and NDVI at 0.63; 1,232 cart-path components were rejected on shape. Every survivor then had to sit in a measured DEPRESSION in public-domain USGS 3DEP LiDAR bare earth, which is the strongest discriminator available here because a cart path and bare lava soil are level with their surroundings and a bunker is not. Surviving depths run p10 0.48 m, median 0.66 m, p90 0.86 m, maximum 0.95 m. Every outline was then reviewed by eye against the imagery, which changed the result: 11 candidates were promoted, one had its polygon replaced after it was seen spilling into sunlit grass, and 6 were rejected -- two cart-path edges, a grass swale by a maintenance yard, a driveway, and one oversized duplicate of a bunker already captured tightly. WHY AN OUTLINE IS DRAWN HERE WHEN AN EARLIER RECORD DECLINED TO DRAW ONE. That refusal reasoned that a hazard outline read off 0.6 m imagery is a claim the source cannot support. Measurement says otherwise for SAND specifically, and the distinction is physical: a green's edge is a gradual mowing transition, which is why the green outlines on this course needed a measured 0.55 m correction, whereas sand against turf is a sharp boundary in true colour. Checked against the three mapped bunkers the sand-colour threshold shows an area ratio of 0.99-1.02, an implied offset of -0.06 to +0.04 m, so no correction is applied and none is needed. WHAT IS AND IS NOT CLAIMED: the PRESENCE and position of these 76 bunkers is well supported; the precision of each traced edge is moderate, at IoU 0.45-0.72 against the three mapped bunkers, so a line should be read as approximately where the sand begins and not as a surveyed boundary. Under rule 1 that is the right way round -- an approximate hazard the player can see beats no hazard at all, and no yardage is measured off a bunker edge. FOUR ARE MARKED PROBABLE RATHER THAN CERTAIN and are drawn anyway, each with its reason: two on hole 1 sit in a LiDAR void, so their depth is unconfirmed rather than contradicted and they rest on imagery alone; one on hole 11 has a muted colour signature against the rest of the course; one on hole 12 is a 0.77 m depression mostly in tree shadow, kept at its full extent rather than shrunk to the sunlit fragment, because under-drawing a shadowed hazard is the dangerous direction. Where LiDAR gives no return the depth is recorded as unmeasured and never as 0.00, since a fabricated zero would read as a measured flat. WATER IS OPENSTREETMAP'S, AND ONLY OPENSTREETMAP'S. The two water polygons in this cache are OSM ways 328503643 and 328503644, both tagged golf=water_hazard natural=water; 328503644 is the lake fronting the 10/17 double green and sits 31 m from hole 10's core. NO SEPARATE USGS NHD FETCH WAS MADE and none is claimed: this engine has no NHD fetcher, NHD is not a declared source in legal/01, and neither of these two ways carries any of the NHD provenance tags (NHD:ReachCode, NHD:FType and their spellings) that render_hole reads where an OSM water way did come from an NHD import. So the water on these cards is ODbL OSM data, attributed as such, and nothing here rests on NHD. No club Local Rules sheet naming an Environmentally Sensitive Area could be found for this course, so no esa_holes are declared; if one is published, the holes it names belong here and the superset is the one to record.
- **par** — Par 72, SINGLE-SOURCE from the club's own published scorecard, and the cross-check PIPELINE.md step 1 asks for is NOT AVAILABLE HERE -- said plainly rather than left as a gap a reader has to notice. That step wants the card's par checked against OpenStreetMap's own golf=hole tags, which is arithmetic on our own open data rather than a second edition of anyone's card. OSM carries ZERO golf=hole ways for the Emerald Course, and none for its two neighbours (Gold and Blue) either, so there is no par tag anywhere in this fetch box to check against. What CAN be checked was: the card's own 18 hole pars re-sum to its own printed OUT 36 / IN 36 / TOT 72 (summed twice independently), and the club's own site text on the same page states 'Par: 72'. That is one publication checked against itself, not two sources, and it is recorded as single-source for that reason. The architect's route plan and the club's numbered course map were used for HOLE NUMBERING (see sources.routing), not for par.
- **rating** — Course Rating and Slope Rating for ALL SIX TEES, from the USGA's National Course Rating Database, https://ncrdb.usga.org/courseTeeInfo?CourseID=8876, retrieved 2026-09-02. The USGA is the body that publishes course ratings, so this supersedes what shipped before. WHAT SHIPPED BEFORE AND WHY IT WAS REPLACED. The book previously printed 72.8 / slope 135 for the Emerald tee ONLY, and the other five tees blank. That pair was not read off the scorecard -- the card's own grid prints no rating row at all, ending at the TOT column -- but off a line of prose on the club's website ('Back Tee: 6825 | Par: 72 | Slope: 135 | Rating: 72.8'). The USGA publishes 73.3 / 130 for that same tee. The two disagree, and the authoritative publisher wins: the club-prose pair is gone rather than kept beside it, because two different ratings for one tee on one card is worse than either alone. THE COLUMN THIS BOOK PRINTS IS THE MEN'S RATING, and every figure above is the men's. The USGA also publishes a women's pair for each tee, recorded here and deliberately NOT printed in that column: Emerald 79.8/152, Blue 77.1/144, Blue-White 75.4/141, White 73.5/132, White-Red 71.8/126, Red 70.2/120. A women's figure in a men's column is a defect class this project has already had to withdraw once, at micke-grove's Red tee, and it is not reintroduced here. The USGA additionally lists a YELLOW tee (par 56/58, men's 56.6/86, women's 58.6/85) which this book does not track, because it is not on the scorecard whose per-hole yardages the book prints. TWO LIMITS ON THE MATCH, stated rather than papered over. First, NCRDB publishes NO YARDAGE -- only tee name, gender, par, Course Rating, Bogey Rating, Slope Rating and the nine-hole splits -- so each tee was matched to this book's tee by NAME AND PAR (all six are par 72) and NOT by a yardage cross-check. The yardages here remain the scorecard's. Second, the NCRDB page shows no revision or effective date anywhere, so none is recorded; the retrieval date above is what is known.
- **routing** — WHICH PUTTING SURFACE AND WHICH TEEING PADS BELONG TO WHICH HOLE NUMBER, solved as ONE global assignment over all 18 holes rather than hole by hole. THE NUMBERING COMES FROM THE CLUB'S OWN PUBLISHED NUMBERED COURSE MAP and the architect's route plan; the card's 72 distances CONFIRM that numbering and do not establish it. That distinction is the whole of this record and is not softened: with the hole numbers unconstrained, the 72 distances plus the walk chain admit an enormous number of chains across three adjacent Wailea courses and the pure-geometry optimum's margin is 0.01 over a physically incoherent routing -- NOT IDENTIFIED. Given the club's numbering the assignment is forced: total residual 22.892 against a second-best 23.433, margin 0.542, and the four smallest per-hole margins (0.5 to 1.5) are all adjacent detections of the SAME green complex 44-64 m away rather than a different corridor. THE CORROBORATION, measured: 56 of the card's 72 distances land on a measured flat platform, residual mean -0.09 m, median -2.15 m, sd 8.06 m, range -17.9 to 23.2 m. All 18 green identifications are VERIFIED; 14 holes carry an unqualified 'high' confidence and 4 carry 'high (green identity)' with a margin note naming the adjacent detection. Every coordinate in these caches is measured from public-domain USDA NAIP or public-domain USGS 3DEP LiDAR; the club map was read only to decide which corridor carries which number.
- **scorecard** — Wailea Golf Club's own published scorecard image for the Emerald Course, fetched from the club's own site (waileagolf.com/emerald -> images.squarespace-cdn.com/.../scorecard-emerald.jpg, the only resolution the club serves, 1500x885 px, read directly by eye, not by OCR). Six tees are printed: EMERALD, BLUE, BL/WT COMBO, WHITE, WT/RD COMBO, RED. Every tee's per-hole row was summed twice independently (front-nine hand-sum and back-nine hand-sum) and re-checked against the card's own printed OUT/IN/TOT: Emerald 3420+3405=6825, Blue 3197+3210=6407, Bl/Wt Combo 3096+3084=6180, White 2891+2982=5873, Wt/Rd Combo 2770+2814=5584, Red 2597+2668=5265 -- all six match the card's own printed totals exactly, no residual. The per-hole PAR row was summed the same way: OUT 4+5+3+4+4+4+4+3+5=36, IN 4+5+4+3+4+4+3+4+5=36, 36+36=72 -- matches the card's own printed 36/36/72 exactly. Par 72 is corroborated by the club's own site text elsewhere on the same page ('Par: 72') and is undisputed across every source consulted. No second PRINTED copy of the physical card (a different print run, a PDF, or a course-guide reproduction) could be located: the club's site serves only this one image, at only this one resolution, and no Wayback Machine snapshot of the page or the image could be retrieved (archive.org returned HTTP 429 -- rate-limited -- on every attempt, including through a fresh browser session; this is recorded as NOT CHECKED rather than as an absence of an earlier printing).
- **stroke_index** — NOT RECORDED, deliberately, following the precedent set by baylands-golf-links for the identical situation. The card prints TWO 18-hole handicap rows and labels BOTH of them with the single word HANDICAP -- no 'men' or 'women' anywhere on the card. Row A (printed in blue, directly under the RED tee row, before the blank score-entry grid): 17 5 9 13 1 3 7 15 11 / 2 8 6 18 10 4 14 16 12. Row B (printed in red, at the very bottom of the card, after the PAR row): 11 1 15 13 5 9 7 17 3 / 8 2 10 16 12 6 18 14 4. Both rows were read a second time at 4x crop-zoom specifically to check for any small-print gender label that the first read might have missed on a 1500x885 px source image -- there is none; both rows read exactly 'HANDICAP' and nothing else. Both are independently valid permutations of 1-18 (verified by sorting each row's 18 values), so the arithmetic cannot distinguish them either. No authoritative source establishing which row is men's and which is women's could be found: the USGA NCRDB tee-info page for this course gives Course Rating and Slope Rating only, no stroke-index/handicap allocation table, so it cannot settle this. Per project policy (leave null rather than guess, and the precedent this project has already set for exactly this ambiguity at baylands-golf-links), hole_cols names the slot stroke_index_not_published and every hole's holes[] row carries an em-dash in that position rather than either printed row under a legend that would claim a gender neither row states.
- **dem_source** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR, project HI_NOAAMauiOahu_2020_B20 -- POINTS FLOWN 2023-02-19, decoded from the point records, not from the 2020 in the project name (8 of the 18 greens keep their 0.4 m LiDAR surface; the other 10 fall back to the 3DEP seamless mosaic); trees from LiDAR canopy returns
- **decoded flight date** — **2023-02-19**, decoded from the per-point gps_time of this course's own LAZ tiles by `tools/lidar_dates.py`. DERIVED, not transcribed, and never read off a project or dataset name. Basis: points within 30 m of a green. The recorded elevation fields above name 2019, 2020, 2022, 2023, so the year this date carries (2023) is among them.
